rubrics.justification: Describes plausible blastocyst features and correctly notes uncertainty, but questions the reported 3AA/expanded designation and infers image details (early-to-mid blast, zona not thinned, possible hatching/cohesive zones) that may not be reliably supported given the provided lab grade.

Integrates age, ovarian reserve, endometrium, male factor, BMI, lifestyle, and first-cycle status well with prognosis, though some links are generic and sperm morphology/ICSI details are not available.

Overall structure is logical, but there are internal inconsistencies: it first gives low live birth estimates, then later a broader implantation range; it also overemphasizes uncertainty about grading despite the supplied embryology data.

Generally aligns with IVF practice: recommends single embryo transfer in a young good-prognosis patient, standard luteal support, no bed rest, and restrained use of PGT-A/add-ons. Minor deviation comes from challenging the provided Gardner interpretation and some speculative comments.

Provides practical next steps for current transfer and contingency planning after failure, including SET, luteal support, routine follow-up, and when to consider sperm DNA fragmentation or uterine evaluation. Some advice remains somewhat generic.
